decisions.structure: CSharp secure-random platform helpers and all modules now consume NativeRuntimePolicy definitions; compiled projection already generated. Native still duplicates the Windows/Linux fill bodies and only declares attribute group0 on socket modules.
decisions.branches: Windows chunk limit/BCrypt status versus Linux partial getrandom progress; empty/failure/success fills; declared random intrinsic and Result owner versus no-random control; explicit nounwind group0 in every emitted CSharp module.
decisions.logic: Native authored adapters will call the existing generated policy definitions and retain all current intrinsic admission, allocation/failure cleanup and return ABI code. Publish RuntimeFunctionAttributes unconditionally at the existing module end to match CSharp: introducing shared helpers carrying #0 must not leave that number available to inferred intrinsic attributes. Both old Native fill bodies equal the old CSharp definitions except their explicit #0 and blank lines; no fill algorithm is changed.
decisions.diagnostics: Current CSharp4 and actual raw LLVM4 pass existing stdout/oracles; group0 remains nounwind and Windows body matches original. No old Native failing execution was newly built; the conditional attribute-group publication and duplicated bodies were confirmed by source inspection. Linux body equivalence is static only; OS/runtime acceptance stays pending.

sourceEmitterBudget.reason: One current CLI for shared secure-random definitions and authoritative group0 after CSharp4, actual source/LLVM inspection, semantic4 and stdlib1; no separate diagnostic or Stage build.
